addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- entire-search: Search Entire checkpoint history and transcripts with `entire search --json`. Use proactively when the user asks about previous work, commits, sessions, prompts, or historical context in this repository. (Tools: Bash)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.content:
1	"""
2	Tool definitions and dispatch.
3	
4	Each tool has two parts:
5	  1. A JSON schema in TOOLS — sent to Anthropic so the model knows what's available.
6	  2. A Python implementation below — called by agent.py's loop after the model
7	     requests the tool. The model never runs Python; your loop does.
8	
9	dispatch_tool(name, inputs) -> str  is the single entry point used by agent.py.
10	"""
11	
12	import csv
13	import os
14	from pathlib import Path
15	
16	import openpyxl
17	import pdfplumber
18	
19	# Maximum characters returned by read_file before truncation.
20	# Keeps individual tool results from blowing out the context window.
21	DEFAULT_MAX_CHARS = 20_000
22	
23	# ── tool schemas (sent to Anthropic) ─────────────────────────────────────────
24	
25	TOOLS = [
26	    {
27	        "name": "read_file",
28	        "description": (
29	            "Read a file and return its text content. "
30	            "Supports PDF, Excel (.xlsx), CSV, and plain text (.txt, .md). "
31	            "For spreadsheets, returns all sheets as tab-separated text. "
32	            "For PDFs, returns extracted text page by page. "
33	            "Large files are truncated to max_chars characters."
34	        ),
35	        "input_schema": {
36	            "type": "object",
37	            "properties": {
38	                "path": {
39	                    "type": "string",
40	                    "description": "Path to the file.",
41	                },
42	                "max_chars": {
43	                    "type": "integer",
44	                    "description": (
45	                        f"Truncate output to this many characters "
46	                        f"(default {DEFAULT_MAX_CHARS}). Increase if you need more."
47	                    ),
48	                },
49	            },
50	            "required": ["path"],
51	        },
52	    },
53	    {
54	        "name": "list_files",
55	        "description": "List files in a directory, showing names and sizes.",
56	        "input_schema": {
57	            "type": "object",
58	            "properties": {
59	                "directory": {
60	                    "type": "string",
61	                    "description": "Path to the directory to list.",
62	                }
63	            },
64	            "required": ["directory"],
65	        },
66	    },
67	    {
68	        "name": "load_skill",
69	        "description": (
70	            "Load the full content of a named skill from the ./skills folder. "
71	            "Use this when you need detailed step-by-step instructions for a "
72	            "specific task type (e.g. financial_analysis)."
73	        ),
74	        "input_schema": {
75	            "type": "object",
76	            "properties": {
77	                "name": {
78	                    "type": "string",
79	                    "description": "Skill filename without the .md extension.",
80	                }
81	            },
82	            "required": ["name"],
83	        },
84	    },
85	]
86	
87	# ── tool implementations ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
88	
89	def read_file(path: str, max_chars: int = DEFAULT_MAX_CHARS) -> str:
90	    if not os.path.exists(path):
91	        return f"Error: file not found: {path}"
92	
93	    ext = os.path.splitext(path)[1].lower()
94	    try:
95	        if ext == ".pdf":
96	            raw = _read_pdf(path)
97	        elif ext in (".xlsx", ".xls"):
98	            raw = _read_excel(path)
99	        elif ext == ".csv":
100	            raw = _read_csv(path)
101	        elif ext in (".txt", ".md", ".json", ".yaml", ".yml", ".toml", ""):
102	            raw = Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
103	        else:
104	            return f"Unsupported file type '{ext}'. Supported: pdf, xlsx, csv, txt, md."
105	    except Exception as exc:
106	        return f"Error reading {path}: {exc}"
107	
108	    if len(raw) > max_chars:
109	        return raw[:max_chars] + f"\n\n… [truncated — {len(raw) - max_chars} chars omitted]"
110	    return raw
111	
112	
113	def _read_pdf(path: str) -> str:
114	    pages = []
115	    with pdfplumber.open(path) as pdf:
116	        for i, page in enumerate(pdf.pages):
117	            text = page.extract_text()
118	            if text:
119	                pages.append(f"--- Page {i + 1} ---\n{text}")
120	    return "\n\n".join(pages) if pages else "No extractable text found in PDF."
121	
122	
123	def _read_excel(path: str) -> str:
124	    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(path, read_only=True, data_only=True)
125	    parts = []
126	    for sheet_name in wb.sheetnames:
127	        ws = wb[sheet_name]
128	        rows = []
129	        for row in ws.iter_rows(values_only=True):
130	            if any(cell is not None for cell in row):
131	                rows.append("\t".join("" if c is None else str(c) for c in row))
132	        parts.append(f"=== Sheet: {sheet_name} ===\n" + "\n".join(rows))
133	    return "\n\n".join(parts)
134	
135	
136	def _read_csv(path: str) -> str:
137	    with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
138	        rows = ["\t".join(row) for row in csv.reader(f)]
139	    return "\n".join(rows)
140	
141	
142	def list_files(directory: str) -> str:
143	    if not os.path.exists(directory):
144	        return f"Error: directory not found: {directory}"
145	    if not os.path.isdir(directory):
146	        return f"Error: not a directory: {directory}"
147	
148	    entries = []
149	    for name in sorted(os.listdir(directory)):
150	        full = os.path.join(directory, name)
151	        size = os.path.getsize(full)
152	        kind = "dir" if os.path.isdir(full) else f"{size:,} bytes"
153	        entries.append(f"  {name:<45} {kind}")
154	
155	    if not entries:
156	        return f"Empty directory: {directory}"
157	    return f"Contents of {directory}:\n" + "\n".join(entries)
158	
159	
160	def load_skill(name: str) -> str:
161	    skill_path = os.path.join("skills", f"{name}.md")
162	    if not os.path.exists(skill_path):
163	        available = [
164	            f[:-3] for f in os.listdir("skills") if f.endswith(".md")
165	        ] if os.path.isdir("skills") else []
166	        return f"Skill '{name}' not found. Available skills: {available}"
167	    with open(skill_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
168	        return f.read()
169	
170	
171	# ── dispatch table ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
172	
173	def dispatch_tool(name: str, inputs: dict) -> str:
174	    """Route a tool call by name. Called by the agent loop — never by the model."""
175	    if name == "read_file":
176	        return read_file(inputs["path"], inputs.get("max_chars", DEFAULT_MAX_CHARS))
177	    if name == "list_files":
178	        return list_files(inputs["directory"])
179	    if name == "load_skill":
180	        return load_skill(inputs["name"])
181	    return f"Unknown tool: '{name}'. Available: read_file, list_files, load_skill."
